Citation / short title: Chriki et al. (2024). Attitudes toward artificial meat in Arab countries
Findings: Willingness and price expectations for cultivated meat.
Limitations / corrections: Pooled attitudes, not national adoption. An earlier draft used ~41% willing to try; abstract says >40%. Correct DOI is 1750-3841, not the earlier 1754-3841.
Access status: Abstract verified; full-text access not established

Citation / short title: Maqsood et al. (2025). Are Emirati consumers in United Arab Emirates open to alternative proteins?
Study type and method: Peer-reviewed survey. Online questionnaire via email/social media
Findings: Plant-based protein preferred over cultivated meat, microalgae and insects.
Limitations / corrections: Preferences, not consumption. Women and ages 18–24 dominate sample; excludes expatriates.
Access status: Open full text and supplementary-material page
Respondent-level data: Article/supplements; further inquiries to corresponding author

Citation / short title: Dean et al. (2023). Should I Really Pay a Premium for This?
Study type and method: Peer-reviewed survey. Email/social media; online and optional paper questionnaire; pooled models
Findings: Perceived suitability and environmental effects were associated with willingness to try, buy and pay more.
Limitations / corrections: Online publication 2023; journal issue 2024. Pakistan/Indonesia sample counts are not consumption rates.
Respondent-level data: Available from corresponding author upon request

Citation / short title: Alptekin et al. (2026). Consumer acceptance of cultured meat and its determinants among Turkish adults
Study type and method: Peer-reviewed survey. Cross-sectional online survey; full sampling detail not assessed
Limitations / corrections: Willingness to try, not consumption. Perceived unnaturalness, safety concerns and distrust were barriers.
Access status: Abstract public; full article subscription-limited; supplementary PDFs public

Citation / short title: Alabdulmohsen and Al-Otaibi (2025). Exploring Novel Foods: Edible Insect Acceptance in Saudi Arabia
Study type and method: Peer-reviewed survey. Online social-media snowball sampling
Findings: Men reported more prior insect consumption than women.
Limitations / corrections: Prior insect consumption by sex. Not evidence about plant-based or cultivated meat. Non-probability recruitment limits generalisation.
Respondent-level data: Published contributions in article; inquiries to corresponding author

Citation / short title: Terano et al. (2023). Exploring Muslim Consumers’ Acceptance of Cultured Beef Meat
Study type and method: Peer-reviewed survey. University-linked sample; 62 online, 40 in-person
Findings: Acceptance varies with attitudes and religious concerns; conflicting headline percentage.
Limitations / corrections: Abstract reports 44.1% acceptance; Table 3 reports 50/102 (49.0%). Table 1 uses 44.1% for awareness. Retain discrepancy; not a national estimate.

Citation / short title: Rakuten Insight (2025). Plant-based food alternatives, June 2025
Population: 12 Asian markets; six Southeast Asian countries extracted
Fieldwork: 2025 report; exact field dates not verified
Study type and method: Commercial market survey. Proprietary online panels, ages 16+
Findings: Six country results answer willingness to eat lab-grown meat.
Limitations / corrections: Country samples do not isolate Muslims. National representativeness not established. Broad plant-food measures include milk; do not treat them as meat consumption.

Citation / short title: GFI APAC / The Good Growth Co. (2024). Decoding Demand
Population: Indonesia; Malaysia; Philippines; Singapore; Thailand; Vietnam
Study type and method: Advocacy-commissioned market research. Regional consumer survey; quantitative sample 5,971
Findings: 5% regular consumption; 44% aware but never tried; 9% unaware; >80% would buy at a 20% discount.
Limitations / corrections: Regional summary, not national estimates. GFI promotes alternative proteins. Price scenario is hypothetical. Frequency threshold for 'regular' not verified.

Citation / short title: Lwin, Malik, Ho and Schulz (2026). Feeding the future
Study type and method: Peer-reviewed survey. Online sample described by authors as nationally representative
Findings: Plant-based protein had highest acceptance; familiarity, expected taste and perceived healthfulness were common correlates.
Limitations / corrections: Journal issue March 2026; first online 2025. Acceptance comparison, not consumption prevalence.
Access status: University publication record and abstract verified
